sentences.text: The known fossils of Agnosphitys consist of an ilium, maxilla, astragalus, and humerus.
Based on the left ilium discovered in 1990, scientists estimate Agnosphitys measured approximately 70 centimeters in length.
The species Agnosphitys cromhallensis was described by Nicholas Fraser, Kevin Padian, Gordon Walkden, and A. L. M. Davis in early 2002.
Fossils of Agnosphitys consist of two distinct specimens.
The holotype specimen is a single isolated left ilium.
The fossils were found in the Magnesian Conglomerate of Avon, England.
According to its describers, Agnosphitys exhibited 5 of the 17 potential synapomorphies accepted for dinosaurs.
In its original description, Agnosphitys was placed outside Dinosauria based on the definition provided by Padian and May (1995).
A 2007 phylogenetic analysis by Yates recovered Agnosphitys as a theropod.
A 2010 analysis by Ezcurra recovered Agnosphitys as a member of the family Guaibasauridae.
Recent studies have considered Agnosphitys to be a silesaurid based on unpublished descriptions of Asilisaurus.
A 2017 large-scale phylogenetic analysis by Baron, Norman, and Barrett recovered Agnosphitys as a member of the clade Silesauridae.
In 2007, José Fernando Bonaparte and colleagues included Agnosphitys in the primitive saurischian family Guaibasauridae.
The genus Agnosphitys contains only one known species, A. cromhallensis.
The fossils date from the Norian and Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic, or possibly the Hettangian stage of the Early Jurassic.
Agnosphitys lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 218 million years ago in the Norian stage, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Agnosphitys is estimated from 237 to 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
While Agnosphitys is considered close to the ancestor of dinosaurs, its exact evolutionary position is disputed by researchers.
Researchers disagree on whether Agnosphitys is a theropod dinosaur more derived than Eoraptor or a dinosauromorph archosaur closely related to dinosaurs.
